title: Space Agencies Report Increased Risk of Space Rock Striking Earth in 2032
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: Scientists say the threat of a large space rock striking the Earth in 2032 has increased.
sentences.zh: 科学家说,2032年大块空间岩石撞击地球的威胁增加了。

sentences.en: Recent calculations suggest there is a small chance - perhaps around 1 to 3 percent - the space rock 2024 YR4 will hit Earth in 2032.
sentences.zh: 最近的计算显示,2024年的YR4号太空岩在2032年撞击地球的可能性很小,可能只有1%到3%左右。

sentences.en: This also means there is around a 97 to 99 percent chance it will safely pass our planet in that year.
sentences.zh: 这还意味着大约97%到99%的概率 它会在当年安全通过我们的星球。

sentences.en: The odds of a strike will likely continue to go up and down as the asteroid’s path around the sun is better understood.
sentences.zh: 随着小行星在太阳周围的路径得到更好的了解,撞击的可能性可能会继续上升和下降。

sentences.en: And scientists say there is a good chance the risk will drop to zero.
sentences.zh: 科学家们说 风险很有可能降到零

sentences.en: NASA and the European Space Agency’s Webb Space Telescope will observe this near-Earth asteroid in March before the object becomes impossible to see.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局和欧洲航天局的Webb空间望远镜将在3月观察这颗近地小行星,然后该天体就无法看到。

sentences.en: Once that happens, scientists will have to wait until 2028 when it passes our way again.
sentences.zh: 一旦发生这种情况,科学家将不得不等到2028年,当它再次经过时。

sentences.en: What is an asteroid? Asteroids are space rocks orbiting the sun.
sentences.zh: 小行星是绕着太阳运行的太空岩石

sentences.en: Asteroids are much smaller than planets.
sentences.zh: 小行星比行星小得多

sentences.en: Scientists believe they are the leftovers from the solar system’s formation 4.6 billion years ago.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为它们是46亿年前太阳系形成的剩余物质。

sentences.en: There are millions of asteroids orbiting the sun between Mars and Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 火星和木星之间有数百万个小行星环绕着太阳运行

sentences.en: That area is known as the main asteroid belt.
sentences.zh: 该地区被称为主要小行星带。

sentences.en: The asteroids sometimes get pushed out of the belt and can end up elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 这些小行星有时会被推出腰带 最终会落到别处

sentences.en: How do scientists follow worrisome asteroids?
sentences.zh: 科学家如何跟踪令人担忧的小行星?

sentences.en: A telescope in Chile discovered the asteroid 2024 YR4 in late December.
sentences.zh: 智利的一个望远镜在12月下旬发现了小行星2024 YR4。

sentences.en: It is estimated to measure between 40 and 90 meters across.
sentences.zh: 估计要测量40至90米之间。

sentences.en: NASA said observations by the Webb space telescope should provide a more exact measurement.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局说,Webb空间望远镜的观测应当提供更精确的测量。

sentences.en: At first, NASA and the European Space Agency put the odds of a strike at just over one percent.
sentences.zh: 起初,美国航天局和欧洲航天局 将罢工的几率 定在1%以上

sentences.en: But later calculations suggested the odds had risen to 2 or even 3 percent.
sentences.zh: 但后来的计算表明 赔率上升到了2%甚至3%

sentences.en: NASA described the likelihood of a strike as “extremely low.” Until scientists have a better understanding of the asteroid’s path around the sun, they warned that the odds will continue to change — and quite possibly fall to zero.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局(NASA)将撞击的可能性描述为“极低 ” 。 除非科学家们更好地了解小行星在太阳周围的路径,否则他们警告说,概率会继续改变 — — 很可能下降到零。

sentences.en: “You don’t have to be worried about anything.
sentences.zh: “你不必担心任何事情。

sentences.en: It’s a curiosity ,” said Larry Denneau. He is a software engineer at the University of Hawaii working with ATLAS, a program to identify asteroids that might endanger Earth.
sentences.zh: 拉里·丹瑙(Larry Denneau)说,这是一个好奇心。 他是夏威夷大学的软件工程师,与ATLAS合作,这是一个识别可能危及地球的小行星的方案。

sentences.en: That effort first spotted the asteroid. Denneau said, “Don’t panic .
sentences.zh: Denneau说,“不要惊慌。

sentences.en: Let the process play out, and we’ll have a for-sure answer.” In 2021, NASA said another possibly worrisome asteroid, Apophis, did not present a risk to Earth.
sentences.zh: 让过程开始,我们就会有一个肯定的答案。 2021年,美国航天局说另一个可能令人担忧的小行星阿波菲斯(Apophis)并没有给地球带来风险。

sentences.en: NASA made the announcement after additional telescope observations ruled out any chance of it hitting Earth in 2068.
sentences.zh: 太空总署宣布 之后,额外的望远镜观测 排除任何机会 它撞击地球 在2068年。

sentences.en: Should we worry about asteroid 2024 YR4?
sentences.zh: 我们该担心小行星2024年4号吗?

sentences.en: Experts say it is too soon to worry about 2024 YR4.
sentences.zh: 专家说,现在担心大约2024年为时尚早。

sentences.en: Paul Chodas is director of NASA’s Center for Near-Earth Object Studies.
sentences.zh: Paul Chodas是美国航天局近地天体研究中心主任。

sentences.en: Chodas said in an email to the Associated Press, “No one should be concerned that the impact probability is rising.
sentences.zh: Chodas在给美联社的电子邮件中说,“任何人都不应担心影响概率正在上升。

sentences.en: This is the behavior our team expected.” Chodas added, “To be clear, we expect the impact probability to drop to zero at some point.”
sentences.zh: 这就是我们团队所期望的行为。” Chordas 补充说, “ 要明确一点,我们预计撞击概率会在某个时候降到零。 ”

sentences.en: Since the asteroid’s size and orbit are uncertain, it is unclear where it might hit and what the possible effects would be should it strike Earth.
sentences.zh: 由于小行星的大小和轨道不确定,因此不清楚它可能撞击到哪里,如果它撞击地球,可能产生的影响是什么。

sentences.en: ESA said, if the asteroid is smaller, the effect might be similar to the Tunguska event that flattened thousands of square kilometers of forest in Siberia in 1908.
sentences.zh: 欧空局说,如果小行星小一点,其影响可能与1908年在西伯利亚平整数千平方公里森林的通古斯卡事件类似。

sentences.en: But if the asteroid is larger, close to 100 meters, the effects “would be significantly worse.” Chodas said once the Webb telescope measures the asteroid’s size, NASA can predict “how serious an impact this asteroid could produce and how difficult a task it might be to deflect this asteroid.”
sentences.zh: 但是,如果小行星更大,接近100米,其影响“会更严重 ” 。 Chodas说,一旦Webb望远镜测量小行星的大小,美国航天局可以预测“小行星会产生多大的撞击,以及使小行星偏转是多么困难。 ”

sentences.en: NASA already has some experience moving an asteroid.
sentences.zh: NASA已经有一些经验 移动一个小行星。

sentences.en: The space agency’s Dart spacecraft hit a harmless asteroid in 2022.
sentences.zh: 2022年,航天局的达特号航天器撞到了一颗无害的小行星。

sentences.en: This was the first planetary defense test of its kind, changing the asteroid’s orbit around its larger companion asteroid.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次进行行星防御试验,改变小行星围绕大小行星的轨道。

sentences.en: I’m John Russell. Marcia Dunn reported this story for the Associated Press.
sentences.zh: 我是John Russell, Marcia Dunn为美联社报导了这个故事。

sentences.en: John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English .
sentences.zh: John Russell改编了它,供VOA学习英语。
